notes: Cereal rye representative. Seeding-rate guidance is 40-90 lb/ac; seed-cost range is anchored to Ohio rye economics and checked against the NRCS Ohio basic cover-crop scenario.
Fall establishment by drill/broadcast. Median is near the Ohio grain-drill custom rate after conversion to USD/ha; wide bounds cover lower-cost broadcast and higher-cost custom establishment.
Spring termination/preparation attributable to rye, including application and chemical/mechanical termination. Does not include routine cash-crop field work that would occur without the cover crop.
Incremental machinery/planting adjustment for conversion to no-till or strip-till. Component values are calibrated so combined median cost is close to the FY2025 Ohio NRCS basic no-till scenario.

Management, learning, setup, and residue-management transition cost. A separate herbicide component is intentionally omitted: the Ohio NRCS herbicide scenario states that cover-crop burndown should be handled under CPS 340 when a cover crop is present.
Incremental soil sampling/testing and analytical cost allocated over treated hectares; range accommodates sampling density and testing frequency.
Development/implementation of the nutrient-management system plus recordkeeping. Component allocation is calibrated to the Ohio NRCS non-organic nutrient-management scenario.
Incremental rate/timing/placement and variable-rate or other application-management cost. Median plus other components approximates the FY2025 Ohio NRCS non-organic CPS 590 cost.
Shaping/grading and associated construction. Median total with vegetation aligns with common FY2025 Ohio NRCS grassed-waterway scenarios; upper tail accommodates wider/deeper waterways or checks.
Seedbed preparation, seed, fertilizer, and establishment operations for waterway vegetation. Separate drainage tile, inlet/outlet structures, and erosion-control blanket practices are not included.
Earthwork for the treatment pool. Median is approximately the FY2025 Ohio NRCS constructed-wetland earthwork-only scenario converted from USD/ac to USD/ha.

Native/hydrophytic vegetation establishment. Median approximates the added cost of Ohio NRCS light planting above earthwork-only; upper tail approaches the dense-planting increment. Separate water-control structures, dikes, and sediment basins are excluded.
